Synthesis:
The current Freddie Mac monthly performance file has 35 columns. Column 22 is Actual Loss Calculation (now named Actual Loss); it is a dollar amount, positive for losses and negative for gains. Its formula is Zero Balance Removal UPB + Net Sales Proceeds + Delinquent Accrued Interest + Expenses + MI Recoveries + Non-MI Recoveries. It applies to zero-balance codes 02, 03, 09, and 15; defect-settlement loans are null. Column 35 is Bankruptcy Cramdown Costs. [1][2]

leaf.thinking:
Beginning A2 now. The openbi-ml-pipeline will be used with a star schema: separate fact and dimension tables, no merging.

Creating the Mortgage LGD project folder and SPEC with a decision brief. The gold layer will be built as a star schema linked to shared raw SFLLD data. Initial dimensions include `dim_loan` for origination attributes and `dim_vintage` for cohort tags.

The star schema now includes `dim_geography`, `dim_product`, `dim_disposition`, and `dim_date`. The fact table `fct_credit_loss` will hold one row per credit event. It links to all dimensions via keys and measures EAD UPB, actual loss, recoveries, expenses, and LGD.

The LGD label is actual loss divided by UPB at disposition. Features will be drawn from origination or default attributes. A5 monthly loan fact tables are out of scope for A2.

A dimension or bridge table for MI coverage is needed. The raw SFLLD column mapping was reviewed to confirm Zero Balance Removal UPB and recoveries are correctly identified.

A discrepancy was found between the raw SFLLD disclosure and sample data. The disclosure labels MI Recoveries as column 14, but the sample shows that position as zero. This requires verification before mapping to the star schema.

leaf.thinking:
Carefully extracting the full 35 column names from the disclosure PDF.

Mapping the first 18 disclosure columns from the sample row. These cover identifiers, delinquency status, loan age, settlement dates, modification flags, zero balance codes, interest rates, UPB, DDLPI, recoveries, expenses, and legal costs.

Columns 19 through 34 are now mapped. These include taxes, insurance, miscellaneous expenses, actual loss calculation, modification costs, deferred payment plans, ELTV, zero balance removal UPB as exposure at default, delinquent accrued interest, servicer name, and bankruptcy cramdown. The Actual Loss formula is being verified against the sample row.

Actual Loss formula verified. LGD is approximately 0.28. Scaffolding the star schema now. dim_loan will hold origination attributes without loss amounts. dim_vintage will track origination year, quarter, and cohort.

dim_geography will store property state and MSA. dim_product will capture occupancy, property type, loan purpose, channel, and eligibility flags. dim_disposition will map zero balance codes to labels such as REO or short sale. dim_date will use a YYYYMM grain with year, month, and quarter. fct_credit_loss will hold one resolved credit loss event per loan, linking to the dimension keys.

fct_credit_loss will store exposure at default, actual loss, recoveries, expenses, and accrued interest. LGD ratio will be calculated as actual loss divided by exposure at default. Flags for MI coverage and downturn vintage will be included, along with loan age at disposition. A thin fct_loan_book fact table is being considered for exposure context, though the defaulted population will drive LGD reporting.

Loan book counts versus losses can be derived from dim_loan and the fact table. The ML model will predict LGD severity for defaulted loans using origination features from dim_loan and dim_product. Default-time LTV may not be cleanly available. Raw data from A1 will be reused via a junction or shared path. A pipeline decision brief is required.

The LGD model targets the credit risk desk for EL and capital overlays. The owner is CRO / credit risk, with Alex as portfolio owner. The label is realized LGD from resolved credit events where Actual Loss is non-null. The baseline is mean LGD by LTV band. Metrics are MAE or RMSE on LGD plus beat baseline. A minimum metric of beating baseline MAE by a set percentage is required.

Out of scope items are EL product, PD, auto pricing, and IRB claim. Alex is the technical owner.

The next deliverables are SPEC.md, STAR_SCHEMA.md, LABEL.md, DECISION_BRIEF.md, ML_PIPELINE.md, build_star_gold.py, dq_mortgage_lgd.py, SOURCE.md, .gitignore, and a state update. The gold build and DQ scripts will run as verification. The OpenBI scaffold may need SemanticModel files. This turn focuses on SPEC, decision brief, and star schema.

The pipeline is being sequenced into Prepare, Fit, and Predict stages. Star schema gold build and DQ are Prepare work. Prediction training is deferred until after the state freeze. The raw data will be accessed through a junction path. The gold builder will scan all origination files to construct dimension tables and the loan dimension first.

The gold builder will scan performance files for credit events where ZB is set and Actual Loss is present. It will keep only the disposition month row per loan, dropping defect settlements with missing actual loss. A thin MI dimension or MI percentage on dim_loan may be added. The star schema relationships are now defined: fct_credit_loss connects to dim_loan, dim_vintage, and dim_geography.

EAD UPB values are very small.

Tiny EAD UPB values with large losses create extreme LGD ratios. The gold build will add an `in_lgd_model` flag for rows with EAD UPB above $1000 and LGD between -1 and 3. Alternatively, extreme rows may be quarantined to a separate table.

Quarantining will happen in the quality stage. Rows with EAD UPB below $1000 or absolute LGD above 5 will be flagged with a `quarantine_reason` and excluded from the modeling set.
